newsitem.title: UK: May UK unit trust sales hit record for month.
newsitem.headline: May UK unit trust sales hit record for month.

text.p: British unit trust sales hit record levels for the month in May, latest data show.
The Association of Unit Trust and Investment Funds (AUTIF) said on Monday net retail sales of unit trusts were 673 million stg in May, up from 528 million stg in the same month last year.
This represents a sharp drop from the 1.6 billion stg net unit trust figure in April, when buyers piled into Personal Equity Plans (PEPs) to beat the tax year deadline.
May net PEP sales were 642 million stg, down from April's 1.6 billion stg but up from 567 million stg last year.

"The continued momentum of unit trust PEP sales is bringing the benefits of long-term investment to an ever wider part of the population, with more than 60 percent of PEP holders now standard rate tax payers," said Philip Warland, director general of AUTIF.
May's record net retail unit trust sales were supported by 207 million stg flowing into UK growth trusts, according to AUTIF.
UK gilt and fixed income trusts also sold well, AUTIF said, with corporate bond PEPs especially favoured.
Sales to institutions were a net 294 million stg in May, down from 506 million stg in April.
Institutions shunned underperforming UK smaller companies, with 85 million stg flowing out of the sector in May.
FTSE Small Cap-Capital Return shares have made a total return of just 0.6 percent in 1997, as compared to 9.4 percent for the FTSE 100.
AUTIF said funds under management jumped to 149 billion stg, up 13 percent since the end of 1996.
The figures cover PEP plans operated by unit trust managers only and not plans operated by all PEP plan managers.
